question: A strategy lead must reconcile three conflicting demand forecasts and explain the reasoning to an executive committee. Which tier fits this work best?
options: A) Whichever tier her colleagues most recently used, so the team's outputs remain consistent.
B) The deepest-reasoning tier, accepting the higher allowance cost, since the value is the reasoning.
C) The default middle tier, because reconciling forecasts is fairly ordinary analytical work for a team.
D) The fastest tier, because the committee needs the analysis quickly and speed is what matters.
correct_answers: B) The deepest-reasoning tier, accepting the higher allowance cost, since the value is the reasoning.
explanations: Incorrect. Consistency of tier is not a goal in itself, and it ignores what this particular task demands.
Correct. When several conflicting inputs must be held together and the argument itself is the deliverable, the extra reasoning depth is what the higher allowance cost buys.
Incorrect. Reconciling contradictory sources and defending the reasoning is precisely the harder end of the range.
Incorrect. Speed is not the binding constraint when the whole value of the piece lies in the quality of the reasoning.
